description: SDWIS Fed is the EPA's system of record for Safe Drinking Water Act data, holding the information that states and other primacy agencies must report on every public water system in the United States. For each system it records name and ID, the city or county served, population served, system type (residential community, transient or non-transient), year-round or seasonal operation and the characteristics of its water sources, together with violations of monitoring and reporting schedules, treatment techniques, Maximum Contaminant Levels and public notification rules, and the enforcement actions taken. The SDWIS Fed Reporting Services let anyone query the data warehouse through report filters and download results, free and without registration, and the EPA Drinking Water Data and Tools clearinghouse links it with service area boundaries, state revolving fund data, unregulated contaminant monitoring and AWIA resilience compliance data. No specific licence is named. Caveats: data are only as complete and timely as state reporting, and primacy agencies' own databases may be more current and detailed; systems are not mapped as networks, and source characteristics are summary fields. Simulation uses: an inventory of water utilities with population served to weight service disruption, compliance history as a proxy for system vulnerability, and linking utilities to hazard exposure through service area boundaries. Related records: EPA public water system service areas (data-epa-public-water-system-service-areas).
